description:
Please build a TRNSYS-based solar domestic hot water (SDHW) system simulation model featuring a tempering valve for outlet temperature control. This project simulates a forced-circulation solar hot water system located in Madison, Wisconsin, USA, and evaluates its short-term dynamic performance during a summer period.

Simulation parameters: The simulation covers approximately 7.3 days during summer (from hour 3624 to hour 3800), with a time step of 0.125 hours (7.5 minutes). Integration and convergence tolerances are both set to 0.001, with a maximum of 30 iterations per time step. The successive substitution solver (Solver 0) must be used, as required by the tempering valve controller and the differential controller.

Weather data: A TMY3-format weather data file is provided, located at "weather\US_WI_MADISON_DANE_CO_REGIONAL_ARPT_[ISIS]_726410.tmy3". The weather data processor uses the Reindl radiation model for computing tilted surface radiation on one south-facing surface tilted at 45 degrees from horizontal, with a ground reflectance of 0.2.

The system is a forced-circulation solar hot water system with tempering valve control. It consists of 1 quadratic-efficiency flat-plate solar collector with second-order incidence angle modifiers, 1 stratified hot water storage tank with variable inlets and uniform losses featuring auxiliary electric heating, 1 variable-speed circulation pump, 1 ON/OFF differential controller with hysteresis (successive substitution control strategy), 1 tempering valve controller, 1 controlled flow diverter, 1 tee-piece flow mixer, 1 time-dependent forcing function for the daily hot water load profile, 1 equation block for computing the actual hot water demand flow rate and cold water supply temperature, and 3 online plotters for visualization.

Flat-plate solar collector: A single quadratic-efficiency flat-plate solar collector with second-order incidence angle modifiers. The collector has a total area of 5 m², installed at a slope of 45 degrees facing due south (azimuth 0 degrees). The collector optical efficiency (intercept efficiency) is 0.8, the first-order heat loss coefficient (efficiency slope) is 13 kJ/(hr·m²·K), and the second-order heat loss coefficient (efficiency curvature) is 0.05 kJ/(hr·m²·K²). The incidence angle modifier uses a second-order model with a first-order coefficient of 0.2 and a second-order coefficient of 0. The collector was tested at a flow rate of 40 kg/(hr·m²), and the working fluid specific heat is 4.19 kJ/(kg·K). The efficiency is based on inlet temperature (efficiency mode 1). One collector in series.

Stratified hot water storage tank with variable inlets and uniform losses: A vertical cylindrical tank with a volume of 0.3 m³ and a total height of 1.8 m, divided into 6 equal temperature stratification nodes (each 0.3 m high). The tank uses variable inlet positions (mode 2), meaning both the hot-side and cold-side flows enter the tank at the node closest in temperature to the incoming fluid, maximizing thermal stratification. The tank loss coefficient is 2.5 kJ/(hr·m²·K) uniformly for all nodes. The fluid is water with a specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K) and a density of 1000 kg/m³. The tank is equipped with two auxiliary electric heating elements operating in master/slave mode (mode 1): the lower element is only enabled when the upper element is satisfied. Both heating elements are located in node 1 (top node) with thermostats also in node 1, set point temperature of 60°C, deadband of 5°C, and maximum heating rate of 9000 kJ/hr each. The boiling point is set to 100°C. Initial node temperatures from top to bottom are: 60°C, 50°C, 40°C, 30°C, 20°C, and 15°C. The hot-side inlet receives heated fluid from the solar collector, and the hot-side outlet (bottom of tank) returns fluid to the collector loop. The cold-side inlet receives cold water from the load-side diverter, and the cold-side outlet (top of tank) delivers hot water to the load. The environment temperature is set to a constant 20°C. Both auxiliary heater control signals are set to constant 1.0 (always enabled, internally controlled by thermostats).

Variable-speed circulation pump: The solar loop circulation pump has a maximum flow rate of 200 kg/hr, a maximum power consumption of 240 kJ/hr, a fluid specific heat of 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), a thermal conversion coefficient of 0.05 (fraction of pump power converted to fluid thermal energy), and a power coefficient of 0.5. The pump flow rate is determined by multiplying the maximum flow rate by the control signal from the differential controller.

ON/OFF differential controller with hysteresis (successive substitution control strategy): This controller governs the solar loop pump. It compares the collector outlet temperature (upper input Th) with the tank bottom temperature (lower input Tl). The pump turns ON when the temperature difference (Th - Tl) exceeds the upper dead band of 10°C, and turns OFF when the difference falls below the lower dead band of 2°C. The controller monitors the tank top temperature for high-limit cut-out at 100°C. The number of oscillations permitted per time step is 5. The controller output feeds back to its own input for hysteresis stability.

Tempering valve controller: This controller manages the flow split between the hot water storage tank and a cold water bypass to maintain a desired delivery temperature. The setpoint temperature is 60°C, the source temperature is the tank top outlet temperature, the tempering fluid temperature is the cold water supply at 15°C, and the operating mode is 1 (heating mode). The controller outputs two fractions: the fraction of flow to be sent through the heat source (tank) and the fraction to bypass the heat source. The number of oscillations permitted is 5.

Controlled flow diverter: This valve splits the incoming cold water demand flow into two streams based on the tempering valve controller signal. One stream (outlet 1) is directed to the storage tank cold side, and the other stream (outlet 2) bypasses the tank. The inlet receives cold water at 15°C with the demand flow rate from the load profile equations.

Tee-piece flow mixer: This component mixes the hot water from the tank top (inlet 1) with the cold bypass water from the diverter (inlet 2) to produce the final tempered hot water delivery stream.

Daily hot water load profile and equations: A time-dependent forcing function defines the normalized daily hot water consumption pattern with three usage periods: morning peak from 7:00 to 9:00 (normalized value 0.000056), midday usage from 11:00 to 13:00 (normalized value 0.000028), and evening usage from 18:00 to 22:00 (normalized value 0.000028). Outside these periods, the consumption is zero. An equation block computes the actual demand flow rate by multiplying the forcing function output by a daily consumption scaling factor of 200 (mdDHW = load_profile_output × 200). The cold water supply temperature is defined as a constant 15°C (TCold = 15).

Output requirements:
1. Solar loop temperatures and flow rates: collector inlet temperature, collector outlet temperature, and solar radiation on the tilted collector surface, along with collector outlet flow rate.
2. Tank thermal behavior: tank top temperature (to load), temperatures of all 6 stratification nodes, tank bottom temperature (to heat source), and auxiliary heating rate.
3. Tempering valve performance: cold water supply temperature, tank hot water outlet temperature, final tempered delivery temperature (after mixing), fraction of flow directed to the tank, and fraction of flow bypassing the tank.
4. Load-side flow distribution: tempered hot water delivery flow rate and bypass flow rate.
